label: Validates that the rows in a table has all its mandatory columns
description: Validates that the rows in a table has all its mandatory columns. This rule uses the `partID`, `<table_name>Table`, <table_name>Required` columns in the dictionary to generate the corresponding cerberus fields.
messageText: Missing mandatory column <columnName> in table <tableName> in row number <rowIndex>

label: Validates a categorical column
description: Validates that the values in a categorical column in a table are part of the category set for that column
messageText: Invalid category <invalid_category_value> found in row <row_index> for column <column_name> in table <table_name>

label: Validates that a primary key is not invalidly duplicated in a table.
description: This rules validates that if two rows have the same primary key, they both refer to the same entry. It does this by checking that the lastUpdated field is different.
messageText: Duplicate entries found in rows <row_indexes> for primary key column <column_name> in table <table_name>

label: Validates that a number value is not less than a minimum value
description: Validates that a number value is not less than a minimum value. Values that are not a number but are coerced into one before proceeding with validation. Non-ceroceable values are reported as an error.
messageText: Value <invalid_value> in row <row_index> in column <column_name> in table <table_name> is less than the allowable minimum value of <min_value>; Value <invalid_value> in row <row_index> in column <column_name> in table <table_name> cannot be coerced into a number

label: Validates that a number value is not less than a minimum value
description: Validates that a number value is not less than a minimum value. Values that are not a number but are coerced into one before proceeding with validation. Non-ceroceable values are reported as an error.
messageText: Value <invalid_value> in row <row_index> in column <column_name> in table <table_name> is a <invalid_type> and was coerced into a number

label: Validates that a number value is not greater than a maximum value
description: Validates that a number value is not greater than a maximum value. Values that are not a number but are coerced into one before proceeding with validation. Non-ceroceable values are reported as an error.
messageText: Value <invalid_value> in row <row_index> in column <column_name> in table <table_name> is greater than the allowable maximum value of <max_value>;Value <invalid_value> in row <row_index> in column <column_name> in table <table_name> cannot be coerced into a number

label: Validates that a number value is not greater than a maximum value
description: Validates that a number value is not greater than a maximum value
messageText: Value <invalid_value> in row <row_index> in column <column_name> in table <table_name> is a <invalid_type> and was coerced into a number

label: Validates that a mandatory column does not have missing values
description: This rule ensures that mandatory columns do not have empty cells. A cell that is empty once trimmed is empty as well. A missingness value states why a value is absent, and is a valid way of populating a mandatory column, so it does not trigger this rule. See the missingness rule.
messageText: Mandatory column <column_name> in table <table_name> has a missing value in row <row_index>.

label: Validates the minimum length of a string type
description: The minLength column in the ODM dictionary documents the minimum that a part should have. This validation implements it.
messageText: Value <invalid_value> in row <row_index> in column <column_name> in table <table_name> has length <invalid_length> which is less than the min length of <min_length>

label: Validates the maximum length of a string type
description: The maxLength column in the ODM dictionary documents the minimum that a part should have. This validation implements it.
messageText: Value <invalid_value> in row <row_index> in column <column_name> in table <table_name> has length <invalid_length> which is greater than the max length of <max_length>

label: Validates type of a value
description: Uses the dataType column to check if a value is the correct type or can be coerced into the correct type
messageText: Value <invalid_value> in row <row_index> in column <column_name> in table <table_name> has type <invalid_value_type> but should be of type <valid_type> or coercable into a <valid_type>.

label: Validates type of a value
description: Uses the dataType column to check if a value is the correct type or can be coerced into the correct type
messageText: Row <row_index> in column <column_name> in table <table_name> is a boolean but has value <invalid_value>. Allowed values are <boolean_categories>

label: Validates an email column
description: The dictionary does not contain any metadata to describe if a column is an email or not. This rule hardcodes the email column within it.
messageText: Invalid email <invalidValue> found in row <rowIndex> for column <columnName> in table <tableName>

label: Validates the missingness values of a column
description: Identifies the missingness values that a column can take on, and reports the columns that can not take on any at all. A column can take on missingness values when the `missingnessSet` column in the dictionary has a value for it, in which case they are the members of that set in the sets sheet (eg. `genMissingnessSet` or `nrNAMissingnessSet`). A value outside that set is not a missingness value in that column and is left to the other validation rules to judge (eg. `NA` in a country column is the country code of Namibia). A primary key column can not take on any missingness value, which is the only case this rule reports, and it applies even when the same column is not a primary key in another table, and even when it has no missingness set.
messageText: Invalid missingness value <invalid_value> found in row <row_index> for column <column_name> in table <table_name>. The allowed missingness values are <allowed_missingness_values>
notes: The missingness values a column can take on are exempt from the other validation rules, including the ones that constrain the shape of a value (eg. invalid_type and invalid_category) and missing_values_found. The values it can not take on are not exempt, since they are not missingness values in that column.
